issues.failure_explanation: The paper says a general quaternion circulant gives an X-shaped matrix under F_{p,m}. Strang's c(T_n) is such a circulant whenever phi_2(T_n) is nonzero. Lemma strangcireiglimitlm only gives a spectrum formula through 2-by-2 blocks G[f_m] and shows block-diagonal structure (diagonal blocks of the form diag(.), diag(.) in each 2-by-2 position). It never shows F_{p,n} c(T_n) F_{p,n}^* is diagonal, and the X-shape remark indicates it is not. The abstract and the lead-in to the lemma therefore claim more than is proved.

failure_location.quote: We show that Strang's circulant preconditioners can be diagonalized by discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'diagonalized' by 'block-diagonalized into 2-by-2 blocks (X-pattern) by F_{p,n}', or restrict the claim to the case phi_2(f)=0.
issues.overall_effect: The headline contrast (Strang diagonalizable, general circulants not) is unsupported. The spectral formulas are unaffected.
issues.title: Claim that Strang's preconditioner is diagonalized by the quaternion Fourier matrix is not supported
issues.why_classification: The repair is a wording and scope correction, but it changes a main advertised contribution; the technical results are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: G[f] is defined with (1,2) entry -phi_2(f) and (2,1) entry conj(phi_2(f)), so it is Hermitian only when phi_2(f)=0. The proof of (i) ends with (1,2) entry +phi_2(f). Only that version reproduces the quadratic form, since -phi_2(T_n) has symbol +phi_2(f) by oddness of phi_2(f). Part (ii) and Theorem quatszegothm need G[f] Hermitian, with lambda_min = check f.

failure_location.quote: It is clear that $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian for each $x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the (1,2) entry of G[f] to +phi_2(f)(x) and propagate the sign wherever G is used.
issues.overall_effect: The statement of (i) is wrong as written, and the Hermitian claim used in (ii) and (iii) fails for the stated matrix.
issues.title: Sign error in G[f]: stated matrix is not Hermitian and disagrees with the proof
issues.why_classification: The proof's final line already gives the correct matrix, so this is a one-sign local fix with no loss.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's stationarity relation, for s'>s the entry E(x(t-s') conj(x(t-s))) equals conj(E(x(u) conj(x(u-(s'-s))))) = conj(eta(s'-s)), not eta(s'-s). So the entries below the diagonal should be conj(eta) and those above eta. The displayed T_n is the conjugate (transpose) of the matrix that actually arises from the normal equations, so (hermqtsystem) is not the system derived from (linearsys). The stated unknown also conflicts with the solved-for vector, since the equations determine conj(alpha_s).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap eta and conj(eta) in T_n (equivalently use f(-theta)) and state the unknown as the conjugated coefficient vector.
issues.overall_effect: The identification of the prediction problem with T_n alpha = w, and the generating function (genf) with t_s=eta(s), is inconsistent. The spectral theory is unaffected because check f and hat f are even.
issues.title: Toeplitz matrix of the prediction system contradicts the stationarity relation
issues.why_classification: A local convention fix suffices; the Toeplitz and spectral results and the examples' check f are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For even n the first column of c(T_n) contains t_k only for |k| <= n/2-1 and a zero at position n/2. The eigenvalues are therefore given by the partial sum f_{n/2-1}, not f_{n/2}. The formula sigma(c(T_n)) = union of sigma(G[f_m](2 pi s/n)) with m=floor(n/2) is false for even n, because it includes t_{n/2} terms absent from c(T_n).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use m=floor((n-1)/2) in the eigenvalue formula (keeping the index range for s), or define v_S with t_{n/2} for even n.
issues.overall_effect: Part (i) is incorrect for even n. The limits in (ii) are unaffected, since both partial sums converge uniformly to f.
issues.title: Partial-sum index m=floor(n/2) is wrong for even n
issues.why_classification: A routine index correction; the limit statement and conclusions are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The eigen-blocks are taken as [phi_1, -phi_2; conj phi_2, conj phi_1] at 2 pi s/n and identified with G[f_m]. But G has (2,2) entry phi_1(f)(-x), and conj(phi_1)=phi_1 is real, so the (2,2) entries differ. The block conj(phi_1(T_n)) is diagonalized by the conjugate of F, so its eigenvalues are indexed by -2 pi s/n, yet the same F is used for all four blocks. The sign of the phi_2 blocks is also wrong. The claimed similarities G(-x)=J^{-1}H_sJ and bar{H}_s=diag(-1,1)^{-1} G diag(-1,1) do not hold (entries compared do not match unless phi_1 is even and phi_2 is pure imaginary). H_s is not Hermitian as defined. The final symmetry sigma(G(2 pi (n-s)/n))=sigma(G(2 pi s/n)) is true, but only by a trace and determinant argument using the evenness of |phi_2|, not by the stated chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the block diagonalization with consistently indexed conjugate blocks, so that the symbols match G. Then prove the symmetry sigma(G(x))=sigma(G(-x)) from equal trace and determinant.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the spectrum formula (i), and of the limits in (ii) that rest on it, is unsound as written. Theorems relying on the bounds on lambda_min and lambda_max of c(T_n) inherit the gap.
issues.title: Spectrum identification and symmetry argument in the proof of the Strang spectrum lemma are invalid
issues.why_classification: The conclusion appears correct and a contained recomputation fixes it, but this is more than a typo-level repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\{\eta(s)\}_{s=0}^{\infty}$ is absolutely summable, we obtain the following

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses Lemma strangcireiglimitlm and Lemma tnminuscstneigcontrllm, both of which require {eta(s)} absolutely summable (a Wiener-class generating function). The theorem is stated for a general generating function with only check f > 0. For a merely L^1 or L^2 symbol the low-rank plus small-norm splitting is not established, and the theorem may fail. The proof also writes the undefined check f_max for hat f_max in the bound on lambda_max(c(T_n)).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds prod_{s=1}^{p}(1+eps-mu_s)/mu_s by q^{4n_0} with q the factor at the lower bound 2 check f_min/(3 hat f_max), for p <= 4n_0. This is valid only if q >= 1, i.e. mu_min <= (1+eps)/2. Since mu_min can be as large as 2/3, q<1 is possible for small eps. In that case q^p >= q^{4n_0} and the inequality direction is wrong. The constant needs max{1,q}.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed C(epsilon) does not justify the bound in the case q<1; the superlinear rate itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Constant in the superlinear convergence bound: product over p factors replaced by 4n_0 factors without checking each factor is at least 1
issues.why_classification: A one-line change to the constant, with the rate and the theorem otherwise unchanged.
